statement.p: Find an arc length parametrization \bf r\it_1(s) of {\bf r}({\it t})=\left\lt e^{t}\sin\mathopen{}\left(t\right),e^{t}\cos\mathopen{}\left(t\right),5e^{t}\right>.
Assume t(s)=0 when s=0, and t'(0)>0.

static.solution:
\bf r\it_1(s)=\bf r\it(\phi(s)) where t=\phi(s) is the inverse of the arc length function. We compute the arc length function:
s(t)=\int^{t}_{0}||\bf r\it'(u)|| du
Differentiating \bf r\it(t) and computing the norm of \bf r\it'(t) gives:
\bf r\it'(t)=\left\lt e^t\sin t+e^t\cos t, e^t\cos t-e^t\sin t, 5e^{t}\right>
=e^t\left\lt \sin t+\cos t, \cos t-\sin t, 5\right>
||\bf r\it'(t)||=e^t\sqrt{(\sin t+\cos t)^2+(\cos t-\sin t)^2+5^2}=e^t\sqrt{2(\sin^2t+\cos^2t)+25}=\sqrt{27}e^t
Thus,
s(t)=\int^{t}_{0}\sqrt{27}e^udu=\sqrt{27}\left.e^u\right|^{t}_{0}=\sqrt{27}\left(e^t-1\right)
We find the inverse function of s(t) by solving s=\sqrt{27}\left(e^t-1\right) for t. We obtain:
\frac{s}{\sqrt{27}}=e^t-1
e^t=1+\frac{s}{\sqrt{27}}
t=\phi(s)=\ln\left(1+\frac{s}{\sqrt{27}}\right)
Thus arc length parametrization for \bf r\it_1(s)=\bf r\it(\phi(s)) is:
\left\lt \left(1+\frac{s}{\sqrt{27}}\right)\sin\mathopen{}\left(\ln\mathopen{}\left(1+\frac{s}{\sqrt{27}}\right)\right), \left(1+\frac{s}{\sqrt{27}}\right)\cos\mathopen{}\left(\ln\mathopen{}\left(1+\frac{s}{\sqrt{27}}\right)\right), 5\mathopen{}\left(1+\frac{s}{\sqrt{27}}\right)\right>
=(1+\frac{s}{\sqrt{27}})\left\lt \sin\left(\ln\mathopen{}\left(1+\frac{s}{\sqrt{27}}\right)\right), \cos\left(\ln\mathopen{}\left(1+\frac{s}{\sqrt{27}}\right)\right), 5\right>
